questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Creating Components”?
options: Creating Components helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
Creating Components means the browser can enforce all permissions without the backend.
Creating Components removes the need for error handling, accessibility checks and tests.
Creating Components should be implemented by copying a snippet without checking the Angular version.
questions.answer_key: Creating Components helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.explanation: Creating Components is a concept in the supplied Angular curriculum. Its correct application depends on the intended behavior, surrounding context and verification.

questions.prompt: How should a learner work with “Generating components with the CLI” in this lesson?
options: Treat “Generating components with the CLI” as a reason to skip the surrounding application context.
Assume “Generating components with the CLI” works identically across every Angular major and runtime.
Use “Generating components with the CLI” to bypass runtime validation of external or user-provided values.
Connect “Generating components with the CLI” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.answer_key: Connect “Generating components with the CLI” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “Generating components with the CLI” under Creating Components. Anchor it in a small example and check the behavior rather than relying on a memorized phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification approach for “Creating Components”?
options: Treat a successful client-side render as backend authorization evidence.
Ignore a failing test if the component looks correct in one browser.
Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
Assume an SVG diagram proves the code compiled and passed tests.
questions.answer_key: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.explanation: Verification evidence should match the running environment. Static teaching snippets are not compiler output, and frontend checks do not replace backend authorization.
